title: The Dizzy climb to the roof
subtitle: 身体健康 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）
meta: 主题语境：身体健康（人与自我·身体部位与健康）　|　核心词汇：dizzy　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 dizzy 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 the keeper wrote of ① a dizzy climb to the roof in the calendar, and everybody in the tower said at once that it was ② dizzier than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the keeper, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the dizzy ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the dizziest climb to the roof anybody in the tower had ever seen, or so the calendar for January 1948 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too dizzy to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the dizzy ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a dizzy height of the tower, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as dizzy as the height of the tower they had once had in the old tower. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was dizzy or not, and he said so.

By 1961 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the calendar. What the line asked for was ⑦ something dizzy, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next tower called the whole plan ⑧ quite dizzy; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the calendar kept the names of the dizzy ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1964, twice over, she wrote of another dizzy climb to the roof in the same calendar, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ dizzier than anybody had expected. ⑩ The dizziest height of the tower in the whole tower, she said in 1966, was the one she could never quite name; the dizzy ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 眩晕（前置定语 a dizzy climb to the roof：1954 年守夜人在年历里记下的那件眩晕的一程）
B. adj. 眩晕／令人头晕（比较级 dizzier than：文中两处，一处比爬上屋顶的一程，一处比预想）
C. adj. 眩晕／令人头晕（最高级 the dizziest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 眩晕（表语 too dizzy to do：母亲觉得它太眩晕，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 令人头晕（前置定语 a dizzy height of the tower：叔叔把整件事称作一桩令人头晕的高度）
F. adj. 令人头晕（同级比较 as dizzy as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩塔的高度相比）
G. adj. 令人头晕（后置定语 something dizzy：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 令人头晕（受程度副词修饰 quite dizzy：那位过路人的评价）

items.q: a dizzy climb to the roof
the dizziest climb to the roof anybody
a dizzy height of the tower
The dizziest height of the tower in

answers.why: dizzy 意为“眩晕”，1954 年守夜人在年历里记下的是“一件眩晕的一程”，此处作前置定语 a dizzy climb to the roof。
dizzy 意为“眩晕”，此处用比较级 dizzier than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
dizzy 意为“眩晕”，年历上 一月 那行字说它是钟楼里最眩晕的一件，故用最高级 the dizziest climb to the roof。
dizzy 意为“眩晕”，母亲认为这件东西“太眩晕了，谁也用不上”，too dizzy to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
dizzy 意为“令人头晕”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩令人头晕的高度”，此处作前置定语 a dizzy height of the tower。
dizzy 意为“令人头晕”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩塔的高度一样令人头晕”，同级比较用 as dizzy as。
dizzy 意为“令人头晕”，年历上那半行字要的是“令人头晕的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something dizzy。
dizzy 意为“令人头晕”，邻钟楼来的那位过路人认为这套计划“相当令人头晕”，quite 修饰原级 dizzy。
dizzy 意为“令人头晕”，1964 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要令人头晕”，故用比较级 dizzier than。
dizzy 意为“令人头晕”，母亲 1966 年说的是“整个钟楼里最令人头晕的那一桩”，故用最高级 the dizziest height of the tower。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1954 年，守夜人在年历里记下了一件眩晕的一程。（a dizzy climb to the roof）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更眩晕。（dizzier than …）
母亲觉得它太眩晕，谁也用不上。（too dizzy to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩令人头晕的高度。（a dizzy height of the tower）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩塔的高度一样令人头晕。（as dizzy as …）
到了 1961 年，年历上只剩半行字：要的是一件令人头晕的东西。（something dizzy）
answers: In 1954 the keeper wrote of a dizzy climb to the roof in the calendar.
Everybody said it was dizzier than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too dizzy to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a dizzy height of the tower.
He said nobody would call it as dizzy as the height of the tower they had once had.
By 1961 the calendar asked for nothing but something dizzy.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 dizzy 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1954 the keeper wrote of a dizzy climb to the roof in the calendar, and nobody forgot it.
It was the dizziest climb to the roof in the tower, or so the calendar says.
My mother thought it too dizzy to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a dizzy height of the tower, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next tower called the plan quite dizzy, and everybody laughed.
The dizzy ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
